## The Creation Care and Sustainable Church Task Force<br>The Episcopal Diocese of Texas

Building on the foundation laid by the 2022–2024 [Creation Care Task
Force](https://www.epicenter.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/176th-Annual-Council-Journal-Volume-II.pdf#page=107),
EDOT commissioned a new team in September 2025 to turn recommendations into
reality. Our mission is to offer congregations the encouragement and practical
tools to engage in active Creation Care, from campus cost savings to
earth-conscious spiritual development.

We focus our efforts in three vital areas: **Mitigation**, **Adaptation**, 
and **Formation**.

### [Mitigation](mitigation.html)
![](images/Mitigation_image.png){width=35%}

**Lowering our impact.** Mitigation is about slowing the progress of climate
change by shrinking our environmental footprint. This includes practical steps
to lower energy consumption, conserve water, and move toward zero-waste
communities.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;*Goal: To be better stewards of the resources we use daily.*

### [Adaptation](adaptation.html)
![](images/Adaptation_image.png){width=35%}

**Building resilience.** While we work to slow climate change, we must also
prepare for its effects. Adaptation involves taking proactive measures to reduce
our vulnerability to climate-related challenges and ensuring our congregations
remain safe, prepared, and resilient.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;*Goal: To protect our people and our properties in a shifting climate.*

### [Formation](formation.html)
![](images/Formation_image.png){width=35%}

**Re-imagining our relationship with Earth.** Meaningful change involves
emotion, thought, and action. We seek to engage all three as our community
consciously considers our relationship with all of God’s Creation, moving away
from a mindset of domination and toward acts of loving and responsible
stewardship.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;*Goal: To honor the Creator by loving and protecting every aspect of God’s creation.*

***

### [Process](Process_guidance.html)
**Making it happen.** Congregations that have successfully implemented a Creation
Care program generally have followed a process that engages people in the congregation, 
understands what should be done, sets goals and plans for how to meet them, and
executes those plans as they are able.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;*Goal: Turn aspirations into actions.*

### [Stories](stories.qmd)
**Others Experiences** Preparation is about more than just technical steps. We invite you to explore these real-world stories from throughout our diocese, highlighting how others are putting resilience into practice, allowing us to better relate to our fellow travelers and their experiences. Additionally, if you have a story to share, please contact us. We want to help spread stories of both successes and failures to all our congregations.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;*Goal: Sharing learnings, both successes and caveats.*
